memoryText: Among those who are near me I will be sanctified, and before all the people I will be glorified.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Leviticus 10:3 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Leviticus 10:3 is a sober verse to hold on a day of rest. It comes right after the deaths of Nadab and Abihu, and it is the explanation God gives for what happened. Do not rush past it.

“Among those who are near me.” God speaks about his priests, and by extension all who draw near to him. Nearness is a privilege. It is also a responsibility. The closer you are to God, the more seriously he takes your obedience.

“I will be sanctified.” To sanctify means to treat as holy. God will be treated as holy, either by willing worship or by his own action. It is not a request. It is a statement about how the world is. He will not be ignored.

“And before all the people I will be glorified.” The worship of God is public. The conduct of those who lead worship is seen by everyone. His glory is at stake in how his people approach him.

For the Christian, the verse is a call to reverence. In Christ we are brought near, closer than Aaron ever was. We are not afraid, because the sacrifice has been made. But we are not casual either. Hebrews says, “let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith” (Hebrews 10:22), and “let us offer to God acceptable worship, with reverence and awe” (Hebrews 12:28).
weekInReview: This week you read the end of Exodus and the beginning of Leviticus. You saw the tabernacle built exactly as God commanded and the glory of the LORD fill the tent. In Leviticus you studied the five main offerings: the burnt offering, the grain offering, the peace offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering. You read the priests’ instructions for each, and you watched the ordination of Aaron and his sons. You saw the glory of God appear, and then you saw the death of Nadab and Abihu. The week taught that God makes a way for sinners to draw near, that he asks for obedience and reverence, and that the nearer we come, the more seriously he is to be honored.
reflectionQuestions: The offerings in Leviticus 1 to 7 teach atonement, thanks, and fellowship. Which of these three do you most need to experience right now?
Jesus fulfills all of the offerings. How is he your burnt offering, your sin offering, and your peace offering? Write down one way each speaks to you.
God said, “Among those who are near me I will be sanctified.” What would it look like for you to approach God with both confidence and reverence this week?
prayerPrompts: Ask God to teach you to draw near with confidence and with reverence.
Thank him for opening the way through Jesus.
Rest in him, and ask him to be honored in your life.
